text:
Maya Patel: quick sync — BrightHealth just pushed for eval-triggered alerts + an Optimize advisor that recommends batching/caching/quantization defaults. They want a pilot in July.
Samir Khan: noted. do we have capacity to fold that into the next pilot slice? sounds like two pieces: alerting (signal + webhook) and the advisor (recommendations + UI).
Jen Lee: i'd separate surface area. eval-alerts = infra + alert rules + integration. advisor = inference heuristics + UX + model/quant guidance. different owners.
Ravi Kumar: +1. Technical constraints: alerting needs per-prompt eval hooks and a rules engine (thresholds, windowing). advisor needs telemetry (latency/cost/quality signals) + a small ML scoring service to pick recs.
Alex Gomez: from field: BrightHealth cares about false positives (no noisy alerts) and explainability of recommendations. they'll accept a 6-week pilot if we can show <5% FP and clear action items.
Maya Patel: launch criteria proposal: 1) eval-alerts: signal fidelity validated on 5k prompt set, FP <= 5% on customer vignettes, webhook + retry logic, documented runbook. 2) advisor: 3 recommended actions (batch size, kv-cache TTL, quant profile) with simulated cost savings >= 10% in 2/3 workloads.
Samir Khan: rough effort estimate: alert infra + rules engine ~3 sprints (infra + QA). advisor backend + heuristics + small UI ~3-4 sprints. some shared pieces (telemetry, rollout flags).
Jen Lee: priorities: do minimal eval-alerts MVP first (webhook + simple threshold), then expand heuristics. That reduces blast radius and enables BrightHealth early learnings.
Ravi Kumar: technical notes — KV cache TTL defaulting: don't set global TTL; recommend per-model heuristics (low-latency, high-duplicate prompts -> longer TTL). quant profile: recommend an int8 profile but warn on LM quality delta > 0.8% on chosen eval set.
Alex Gomez: BrightHealth will provide a small labeled eval set (2k) and engineering time for onboarding. They prefer canary rollout to 5% tenants with automatic rollback.
Maya Patel: action items: @Samir to draft acceptance matrix by EOD Wed; @Ravi to prototype TTL heuristic pseudocode and quant guardrails by next Tue; @Jen to sketch alert UX + webhook schema by Fri. I'll coordinate pilot legal + support ask.
Samir Khan: taking acceptance matrix. early thought on SLOs: alert latency <= 2s (from eval hook), webhook retry count 3, and alert precision > 95% on labeled set.
Jen Lee: UX note: alerts should include "why" (metric delta, baseline, sample prompts) and recommended next steps (tune batch size to X, enable quant profile Y). Include copy for customer-facing explanation.
Ravi Kumar: prototyping snippet for TTL heuristic (pseudocode):
```
if duplicate_rate > 0.2 and p99_latency < 150ms:
  recommend_kv_ttl = min(600, duplicates_window_secs)
else:
  recommend_kv_ttl = 0  # disable
```
Also quant gating: run 100-shot eval on customer set, if quality_drop < 0.8% and latency_improve > 15% then recommend int8.
ProductBot: :robot_face: new pilot created: "BrightHealth Optimize Pilot" assigned to maya.patel, samir.khan; target start 2026-07-01.
Maya Patel: risk check: monitoring/ops burden — we need a playbook for noisy alerts and quick rollback. Recommend we instrument an "alert-suppress" flag per-customer and a metric to track alert churn.
Alex Gomez: field request — include a CSV export of alerts and recs for their audit team. Also they need role-based access for turning recommendations on/off.
Samir Khan: noted. will fold RBAC into pilot constraints (admin toggle). Acceptance matrix will include CSV export test.
Jen Lee: timeline proposal: slice A (eval-alerts MVP + webhooks + runbook) = 6 weeks. slice B (advisor recommendations + UI + simulations) = next 6-8 weeks. Pilot gating: BrightHealth sign-off on slice A to proceed to B.
Maya Patel: budget ask for dedicated eng time and 2 GPUs to run quant sims for 2 months. i'll raise to eng managers today.
Ravi Kumar: one more engineering note — ensure recommendations have a confidence score and rollback suggestion. If confidence < 0.6, surface as "investigate" not automatic.
Alex Gomez: thanks — i'll confirm BrightHealth's readiness and ask for the labeled set timeline.
Maya Patel: thanks team. follow-ups: Samir (acceptance matrix by Wed), Jen (alert UX Fri), Ravi (heuristics Tue). i'll schedule a short pilot kickoff with BrightHealth next week. :calendar:
